key_insight: A cognitively grounded small-language-model framework can generate more realistic SUD patient dialogue by aligning responses with latent beliefs, coping strategies, and readiness to change.
clinical_relevance: This could support safer, lower-cost, and more deployable dialogue systems for substance use disorder counseling in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
method: Two-stage pipeline: cognitive component detection followed by cognitive-aligned dialogue generation.
Training strategy combines teacher-model distillation, human-preference optimization, and attention-guided reward shaping.
Targets patient histories and counselor questions to better realize cognitive states in generated responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements on BERTScore, ROUGE, METEOR, BLEU, and LLM-as-judge hit-metrics versus generic instruction-tuned and mental-health-specific SLM baselines, with especially strong gains for open-ended cognitive components.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on annotated preferences, teacher models, and clinically grounded labels, real-world deployment still needs careful validation for bias, privacy, and fidelity to patient behavior.
paper_title: Multi-Objective Aligned Small Language Model Framework for SUD Patient Dialogue Generation
